long_biography.plain_text:
Grendene's evolution from moulded plastic components into branded footwear defined Alexandre Grendene Bartelle's industrial career. The company first made protective baskets for wine bottles, then agricultural parts, soles and heels before developing complete injected-plastic shoes. Its vertically integrated system brought mould-making, PVC production, factories and distribution within one operating structure.

Bartelle served as chief executive through Grendene's expansion and public listing, helping shape its technology, products and design. He left the executive role in 2013 but retained strategic control as board chairman and largest individual shareholder. That separation matters: professional managers run daily operations, while Bartelle's continuing influence rests on founding ownership and board leadership.

uncertainties.detail: Official Grendene filings consistently use Alexandre Grendene Bartelle as the complete name. Grendene Bartelle is the surname sequence, not evidence of a missing middle name. Shortened references such as Alexandre Grendene, Alexandre Bartelle and Alexandre G. Bartelle are treated as abbreviations of the same identity.

The source record stores 2 January 1950, and the English Wikipedia page is internally inconsistent between 2 and 23 January. Grendene's official 2025 reference form and a detailed government biographical record both give 23 January 1950, so the birth-day correction is proposed at 100 confidence.

Grendene's current management page identifies Alexandre, his grandfather Pedro Grendene and his twin brother Pedro Grendene Bartelle as founders. The 2004 prospectus foregrounds Alexandre and his grandfather. The biography follows the current official account and does not assign individual credit for every founding act.

Bartelle has documented investments in furniture, steel, agriculture, ethanol, hospitality, communications and real estate. Grendene nevertheless remains his largest clearly documented current operating interest: he chairs it and owns 44.14%, the largest individual stake. Fashion & Retail therefore remains the best-supported primary industry rather than Diversified.

The dossier uses Grendene's official share percentage only to establish current ownership and influence. It does not convert Grendene's market capitalisation, factories, brands, production capacity or other corporate assets into Bartelle's personal net worth. Billionaire status comes solely from Forbes.

Bartelle was chief executive until April 2013 and remains chairman. Current Grendene material lists separate executives responsible for daily management, so the dossier describes board and ownership influence without presenting him as the current chief executive or day-to-day operator.

The exact Forbes profile and official Grendene company website are verified and proposed. No sufficiently supported personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was found, so none is proposed.
